name: Heidelberg spiking datasets
description: Spiking neural networks are the basis of versatile and power-efficient information processing in the brain. Although we currently lack a detailed understanding of how these networks compute, recently developed optimization techniques allow us to instantiate increasingly complex functional spiking neural networks in-silico. These methods hold the promise to build more efficient non-von-Neumann computing hardware and will offer new vistas in the quest of unraveling brain circuit function. To accelerate the development of such methods, objective ways to compare their performance are indispensable. Presently, however, there are no widely accepted means for comparing the computational performance of spiking neural networks. To address this issue, we introduce two spike-based classification datasets, broadly applicable to benchmark both software and neuromorphic hardware implementations of spiking neural networks. reputation: A niche but useful benchmark for spiking neural network and neuromorphic hardware evaluation, cited mainly within the SNN research community.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; relatively small and specialized dataset, with results depending on the chosen spike-based preprocessing and model/hardware setup.
